children: New U.S. patent covers the moment shopper behavior at the shelf becomes a priced, personalized offer on the shopper's phone. Priority chain runs back to 2013.
CORNELIUS, N.C., Sept. 03, 2026
-- U.S. advertisers are expected to spend $71.09 billion on retail media in 2026.1

) today announced that the United States Patent and Trademark Office has issued U.S. Patent No. 12,725,176 to its subsidiary, Alpha Modus, Corp., covering how a shopper's behavior inside a physical store becomes a priced, personalized offer delivered to that shopper's phone.

The patent, titled "Method for Personalized Marketing and Advertising of Retail Products," is the company's 13th granted U.S. patent. Its priority chain runs back to a provisional application filed in July 2013, years before retail media networks became a standard line item in brand budgets.
What the Patent Covers

The claims describe a two-system method. One system watches what a shopper actually does with products in a store. A second system determines where that shopper is and delivers the offer. Specifically, the patent covers the ability to:
Identify the products a shopper is engaging with by tracking their position at the shelf, tracking their eye movements, or capturing a direct interaction with a kiosk, display, tablet, or phone
Build an information analysis of that shopper's activity, including demographic and sentiment data
Hand that analysis to a separate tracking system that determines where the shopper is located

Deliver a personalized product communication to a mobile device, kiosk, or sales associate, covering price, in-store product placement, advertising content, printed or digital coupons, and limited-time price reductions
Present more than one store location where the product can be purchased, along with the price at each location
Route the resulting purchase to shipping or to in-store pickup

The mechanism sits at the center of how first-party in-store data gets monetized. A retailer or brand observes behavior at the shelf and turns it into a specific offer, at a specific price, at a specific store, on the device the shopper is already holding.
"Retail media spent a decade learning how to talk to shoppers online. The hard part was always the store," said
William Alessi, Chief Executive Officer of Alpha Modus Holdings, Inc.
"This patent covers the handoff: behavior at the shelf on one side, a priced offer in the shopper's hand on the other. We filed on that idea in 2013, and our prior art dates back to that."
A Robust and Defensible Portfolio

Alpha Modus now holds 13 granted U.S. patents with one application pending. The portfolio covers real-time consumer behavior analysis, personalized in-store marketing, shelf and planogram intelligence, inventory management, and customer assistance. As previously announced, the company defeated a motion to dismiss brought by MNTN in August 2026.
The most recent prior issuance in the same family, U.S. Patent No. 12,591,901, was granted on March 31, 2026.
The Alpha Modus, Corp. patent portfolio can be consulted at https://amc.alphamodus.com/.

About Alpha Modus Holdings, Inc.
Alpha Modus Holdings, Inc. ("Alpha Modus" or the "Company")

is a vertical AI company focused on real-time, in-store shopper engagement and attribution. Its patented "closed-loop" retail AI framework, Sense → Decide → Deliver → Attribute, enables brands and retailers to measure the full impact of digital content, physical interactions, and transaction outcomes. Through subsidiaries like Alpha Modus, Corp. and Alpha Modus Financial Services, LLC., the company is actively deploying technologies that merge artificial intelligence, retail media, and financial access across the physical retail landscape.
